title: Increasing the throughput of crystallization condition screens: Challenges and pitfalls of acoustic dispensing systems
author: Kryštůfek, Šácha

steps.title: Equilibrate condition source plate
steps.instruction: Allow the prepared crystallization condition source plate to reach room temperature before any handling.

steps.title: Centrifuge condition source plates
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the source plates for 2 min at 1500 × g to collect condensed fluid on the seal and level the well contents. This step must be performed before any transfer to avoid inconsistencies.

steps.title: Load protein sample into source well
steps.instruction: Dispense the protein sample into a single well of an Echo‑compatible plate that will serve as the protein source.

steps.title: Configure screen condition transfer protocol
steps.instruction: Create a new Echo 550 protocol using Custom Mapping mode combined with a Replication (Source‑Destination interleave) to transfer a screen‑set quadrant to the desired sub‑well. Select the ultrasonic transducer power calibration 384PP_AQ_CP (384‑well polypropylene plate, aqueous conditions) for the lowest error rate.

substeps.instruction: Open Echo 550 software and start a new protocol.
Add a Replication step with Source‑Destination interleave for the quadrant transfer.

steps.title: Transfer screen conditions to destination plate
steps.instruction: Execute the protocol from step 4 to transfer the crystallization conditions onto the destination plate, ensuring a final drop size of at least 50 nl (i.e., 25 nl condition volume for a 1:1 v/v ratio).

substeps.instruction: Run the protocol on the Echo 550.
Verify that each drop contains ≥50 nl total volume (25 nl condition + 25 nl protein later).

steps.title: Configure protein transfer protocol
steps.instruction: Set up a protein‑transfer protocol analogous to step 4 but use the faster calibration setting 384PP_AQ_BP2 for protein samples.

substeps.instruction: Create a new protocol in Echo 550.
Use Custom Mapping and Replication as before.

steps.title: Add protein to condition drops
steps.instruction: Using the protocol established in step 6, dispense the protein solution onto the previously transferred condition drops.

steps.title: Cover plate to prevent evaporation
steps.instruction: Immediately after the plate is ejected from the instrument, cover it with a sheet of glass or plastic to limit evaporation.

steps.title: Fill reservoir wells with storage block
steps.instruction: From a prepared 96‑well storage block, add 30 µl of reservoir solution to each reservoir well. Do not use the Echo for this step because of long transfer times and volume limits (up to 20 µl in Swissci 96‑well low‑profile plates). Note that a 384PP source plate can hold enough volume for only two plates with 20 µl including dead volume.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the 96‑well storage block containing reservoir solution.
Pipette 30 µl into each reservoir well of the destination plate.

steps.title: Seal plate with foil
steps.instruction: Seal the completed plate using microplate sealing foil to maintain humidity and prevent further evaporation.
